nodes.name: Every Hour
nodes.notes: Hourly sweep. Enforces the 48h silence timeout that the reply handler (event-driven) cannot: a lead that goes quiet never triggers 02.

nodes.name: Close Stale Leads
nodes.notes: PATCH qualifying leads whose updated_at is older than 48h -> dead. updated_at is auto-touched on every lead update, so it tracks last conversation activity. return=representation => body is the array of closed rows for per-lead logging. A reply within 7d can still reopen a dead lead (02 re-engagement branch).

nodes.notes: One run_logs row per auto-closed lead (observability, production standard 4).

nodes.name: Find Nudge Candidates
nodes.notes: Leads silent 24-48h, not yet nudged. The 48h upper bound keeps this DISJOINT from the close sweep, so a lead is never nudged and closed in the same hour. conversations(...) is embedded so the transcript arrives in one call (no N+1). limit 50 caps the hourly batch (production standard 8).

nodes.name: Load Send Windows
nodes.notes: All country send-window rows in one call, used to test each lead's LOCAL time.

nodes.name: Select Nudgeable Leads
nodes.notes: Filters candidates to those whose LOCAL time is outside quiet hours (22:00-08:00 per country, wrap-around handled). A batch sweep cannot use 01's Wait-node pattern - parking the hourly cron would stall it - so out-of-window leads are just left for the next run. DELIBERATELY ignores weekend_days: the nudge window is only 24-48h, so skipping a Gulf Fri-Sat or Levant Sat-Sun would mean many leads are closed having never been nudged. Prayer-time delay is also skipped: a non-urgent follow-up does not justify an aladhan call per lead per hour.

nodes.name: Build Nudge Request
nodes.notes: Haiku 4.5 writes the nudge fresh per lead so it can reference what was actually discussed. Carries every lead field forward alongside anthropic_body so downstream nodes never need a second lookup. Cultural rules mirror prompts/conversation-handler.md.

nodes.name: Generate Nudge (Haiku)
nodes.notes: 20s timeout, 2 retries, Continue-On-Fail. A model outage must not stop the nudge - Parse Nudge falls back to a static per-language template and flags nudge_degraded.

nodes.name: Parse Nudge
nodes.notes: Extracts the text block. On any failure falls back to a static per-language template (ar/fr/en) and sets nudge_degraded=true, which the run log records as status=partial. The Arabic fallback string is pending native review.

nodes.name: Send Nudge
nodes.notes: Continue-On-Fail: a Twilio outage must never stop the lead being marked as nudged, or the sweep would retry the same lead every hour.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ lead_id: $('Parse Nudge').item.json.lead_id, direction: 'outbound', channel: 'whatsapp', message: $('Parse Nudge').item.json.nudge_message, twilio_message_id: ($json.sid || null), turn_number: ($('Parse Nudge').item.json.turn_count + 1) }) }}

nodes.name: Log Nudge Outbound
nodes.notes: The nudge becomes a normal outbound conversation row, so it appears in the transcript the scorer and any later turn will read. turn_number continues the existing count.

nodes.name: Mark Nudged
nodes.notes: Idempotency guard: nudged_at IS NULL is the candidate filter, so this is what stops the same lead being nudged every hour. Safe against the silence clock only because migration 004 made the leads trigger ignore nudged_at-only writes - without it this PATCH would push updated_at forward and delay the 48h close to 72h.

parameters.content:
## Nudge at 24h, close at 48h

The close branch (below) used to be the whole workflow: a silent lead went straight to `dead` after 48h and **never heard anything** - the conversation just stopped.

This branch sends ONE Haiku-written follow-up at 24h that references what the lead was actually discussing, then the close branch still closes at 48h if they stay quiet.

**Why the two branches can't collide:** candidates are bounded to `updated_at` between 24h and 48h ago, and the close sweep only takes leads older than 48h. Disjoint sets.

**Why it doesn't nudge twice:** `nudged_at IS NULL` is part of the candidate filter, and `Mark Nudged` sets it. Migration 004 makes the `leads` trigger ignore `nudged_at`-only writes, so marking a nudge does NOT reset the 48h silence clock.

**Quiet hours are respected, weekends are not** - a 24-48h window cannot survive a two-day weekend skip without leads being closed unnudged.
